title: Regulatory Legal Counsel, EMEA
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars. 

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to understand the universe and help expand humanity’s knowledge and capabilities. We work across the full Super Intelligence stack: compute (Colossus supercomputers), models (Grok), and applications (Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X). We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As Regulatory Legal Counsel, EMEA, you will advise on platform, AI and digital regulation that shapes how X, Grok and other SpaceXAI products are built and operated across Europe, the UK, the Middle East and Africa. Europe and the UK have some of the most demanding and actively enforced regulatory regimes we face, including the EU Digital Services Act, the UK Online Safety Act and the EU AI Act. You will turn complex obligations into clear, practical advice and implementation plans, and work hand in hand with Safety, Product, Engineering, Policy, Compliance and our other Legal teams to deliver them.

This role is for someone who enjoys being close to how products actually work, can move quickly between legal analysis and practical implementation, and is comfortable engaging with regulators.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Advise on implementation and compliance with EU, UK and other EMEA digital regulations, with a focus on the EU AI Act, Digital Services Act (DSA), the UK Online Safety Act (OSA), the Audiovisual Media Services Directive (AVMSD) and national implementations such as Ireland's Online Safety Code, and of the eCommerce Directive.

• Support regulatory engagement and investigations with the European Commission, the EU AI Office, Ofcom, Coimisiún na Meán and other regulators, including requests for information, risk assessments, audits, consultations, transparency reporting and enforcement proceedings.

• Work cross-functionally with Safety, Product and Engineering to assess new features and AI products against regulatory requirements, including systemic risk and illegal content risk assessments, age assurance and protection of minors, content moderation and user reporting flows, advertising transparency, researcher data access, and AI transparency and labeling obligations.

• Track and analyze new legislation, codes of practice, guidelines and enforcement trends across EMEA, and explain what they mean for our products in clear, practical terms.

• Help build scalable processes, templates and playbooks for regulatory compliance and product review.

• Partner with Compliance, Product Counsel, Privacy, Litigation and Policy colleagues to keep positions consistent across jurisdictions and regulators.

• Manage outside counsel effectively and cost-consciously.

• Selflessly and generously support what is needed in the legal department, even if it is unfamiliar.

• Adopt daily use of our AI products to accelerate learning and optimize productivity.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Qualified lawyer of good standing ideally UK and/or EU

• Ideally 5+ years of legal experience in technology, platform or digital regulation, at a top-tier law firm, in-house at a technology company, or at a regulator.

• Strong working knowledge of the DSA and/or UK OSA; we don't expect every candidate to have deep experience in every framework listed above, but some combination thereof.

• Strong understanding of the legislative process and the technology industry.

• Exceptional communication skills and the ability to explain complex ideas in a succinct and impactful manner.

We are seeking an experienced remote Healthcare Administrator to provide essential behind-the-scenes patient and billing administrative support across both Sydney allied health clinics. In this role, you will take ownership of patient communications, inbox management, diary rebooking, and invoicing, allowing the on-site team to focus fully on in-clinic patient care. Requirements
Patient Communication & Inbox Management

• Proactively follow up with patients regarding missed appointments, outstanding forms, and referral paperwork.

• Answer and return phone calls as needed (for candidates with strong spoken English).

Billing, Invoicing & Claims Management

• Prepare and issue accurate patient invoices, keep account records updated, and follow up on outstanding balances.

Cliniko Administration & Reporting

• Maintain and update Cliniko system settings, including fee schedules, billable items, pricing, and appointment types.

• Generate and distribute regular operational reports (e.g., revenue, appointment volume, and billing summaries) for leadership.

• Organize and maintain patient medical records, referrals, and administrative documents while adhering strictly to privacy and data security standards.

Operational Support

• Relieve on-site front desk staff of routine back-office administrative tasks.

• Execute additional administrative duties as assigned by the Practice Manager.

QUALIFICATIONS:

• Cliniko Expertise: Direct, hands-on experience managing Cliniko, including setup and maintenance of billable items, pricing, appointment types, and reporting features.

• Healthcare Admin Experience: Proven background in client communication and administration within an Australian clinic setting (preferably allied health, physiotherapy, or medical practices).

• Funding Scheme Knowledge: Working understanding of Australian healthcare funding models, including HICAPS/private health funds, Medicare (EPC referrals), WorkCover, CTP, and DVA.

• Administrative Skills: Demonstrated capability in managing patient email inboxes, complex diary rescheduling, and invoicing workflows.

• English Proficiency: Exceptional written English skills with a warm, empathetic, and professional communication style.

• Shift Availability: Must be fully available to work a split-shift schedule during Sydney business hours from the Philippines.

Preferred:

• Confident spoken English capabilities for direct patient phone contact and call handling.

• Current or recent experience working directly with an Australian healthcare clinic.

• Familiarity with VOIP phone systems, call routing, and live call transfers.

• General proficiency with related operational platforms such as Xero, Microsoft 365, or Google Workspace.

Clinical Research Associate II & Senior Clinical Research Associate (CRA II/Sr. CRA) Multiple Therapeutic Areas | Nationwide Opportunities
IQVIA is actively seeking experienced Clinical Research Associates II (CRA II) and Senior Clinical Research Associates (Sr. CRA) to support a range of clinical studies across multiple therapeutic areas nationwide. This is an exciting opportunity to join a global leader in clinical research and play a vital role in advancing innovative therapies that improve patient outcomes.
In this role, you will be responsible for overseeing clinical trial sites to ensure studies are conducted in compliance with study protocols, regulatory requirements, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), International Council for Harmonization (ICH) guidelines, and sponsor expectations. Successful candidates will possess strong site management skills, a commitment to quality, and the ability to build productive relationships with investigators and site personnel.
Key Responsibilities

• Conduct all phases of site monitoring activities, including site selection, initiation, routine monitoring, and close-out visits.

• Evaluate site performance and ensure adherence to study protocols, GCP, ICH guidelines, and applicable regulatory requirements.

• Partner with investigative sites to develop, implement, and track patient recruitment and retention strategies that support enrollment goals.

• Deliver protocol-specific training and maintain ongoing communication with site staff to ensure alignment on study expectations and timelines.

• Identify, document, and escalate quality or compliance concerns while supporting timely resolution of issues.

• Monitor study progress by tracking regulatory submissions, approvals, enrollment metrics, CRF completion, and data query resolution.

• Ensure essential study documentation is complete, accurate, and maintained within the Trial Master File (TMF) and Investigator Site File (ISF).

• Prepare comprehensive monitoring reports, follow-up letters, and other required study documentation in accordance with company and sponsor standards.

• Collaborate cross-functionally with project teams to support study execution and achievement of project milestones.

• May participate in study start-up activities, site budget tracking, financial management, and site payment processes, depending on assignment.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Life Sciences, Healthcare, Nursing, or a related field preferred. Relevant education and professional experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.

• Minimum of 2 years of independent on-site monitoring experience within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or CRO industry.

• Strong understanding of clinical research processes and regulatory requirements, including GCP and ICH guidelines.

• Knowledge of therapeutic areas and clinical trial protocols gained through industry experience and training.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, as well as mobile and electronic data capture technologies.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to effectively interact with investigators, site personnel, sponsors, and internal stakeholders.

• Strong organizational, problem-solving, and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• Demonstrated ability to work independently while maintaining strong collaborative relationships with colleagues, clients, and study teams.

Join IQVIA and contribute to groundbreaking research while advancing your career with a global leader in healthcare and clinical development. Qualified candidates with experience across a variety of therapeutic areas are encouraged to apply.

title: Head of Financial Control
description:
ABOUT MOTORWAY

Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. We’re looking for an experienced and enthusiastic Head of Financial Control. You’ll own financial control, statutory and tax compliance, treasury and finance operations for the whole company, reporting directly to the VP Finance. You’ll be accountable for the integrity of our numbers, for a control and compliance framework that stands up to audit and diligence, and for the finance systems that let us scale without adding headcount. You’ll work closely with Product, Engineering, Legal and Operations, and own our relationships with auditors, tax advisers and HMRC.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

- Own the integrity of Motorway’s numbers: month-end and year-end close, management accounts and IFRS statutory accounts, and the reconciliations and reviews behind them, so the exec team and board can rely on them without question

- Set and own the control environment: financial controls, policies and delegated authorities that scale with the business, hold up to audit and keep us diligence-ready for any future transaction

- Lead the audit and adviser relationships: plan and run the annual audit, and manage external accountants, tax and legal advisers

- Own treasury and cash: cash flow forecasting, working capital, banking relationships and payment controls, and the cash impact of commercial and operational decisions

- Be accountable for the end-to-end payments, receivables and payroll cycle, setting the standards and controls the team runs to

- Own NetSuite and the finance systems stack, and lead the move to an automated, AI-native finance function

- Lead and develop the team: hiring, coaching, performance and succession across managers and individual contributors

ABOUT YOU

- Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent) with substantial post-qualification experience

- Experience in a technology, marketplace or high-growth business, ideally one with high transaction volumes

- Experience leading an AI or automation change in a finance function: redesigning how work gets done, not just adding tools to the existing process

- A record of leading finance teams through growth and change and developing the people in them, with experience of both operational finance and strategic or transformation roles, and a solid grounding in project management

- Hands-on experience of month-end close, reconciliations, and management and statutory reporting under IFRS or UK GAAP

- Working knowledge of UK tax compliance (VAT, PAYE, R&D relief) and experience managing advisers and HMRC correspondence

- Experience owning a cloud ERP such as NetSuite, automating manual finance processes and using data and AI tools

- A strong grasp of working capital and cash flow forecasting, and of the cash impact of operational decisions

- Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain finance to colleagues outside the function and to the executive team and external stakeholders

title: Software Engineering Manager
description:
​
​

Job Description - Software Engineering Manager
Reports To - Director of Engineering
Summary
AxisCare is hiring a full-time, fully remote Software Engineering Manager to build and lead high-performing engineering teams and to help us reimagine how software teams work in the age of AI.
You've been a software engineer, so you know what it takes to build software. But your true calling is creating the environment where engineers thrive, succeed, and grow.
That job is changing fast. We're no longer coding everything by hand. We're building the systems that let us bring great ideas to life and solve real customer problems quicker than ever before. (Read more about how we think AI is changing product development.)
There will always be a need for people who deeply understand our customers' most important problems, solve them with high-quality software, and run that software reliably in production. That's the work that endures, and you'll be building and leading the teams that do it.
We're looking for a manager who's already internalized this shift. Someone who pushes their team to use AI tools aggressively, but who also has the judgment to know when the AI is producing confident-sounding garbage, and who's building that same judgment in their engineers. Someone who helps their team develop taste and discipline, not just speed.
What You'll Do
Own the day-to-day health of your teams. Help engineers develop great daily habits, strong communication, and reach the next level, including helping them grow from engineers who only write code into engineers who direct AI effectively.
Partner with product and design counterparts to quickly get from "important customer problem" to "working software," favoring rapid iteration over upfront resolution of every ambiguity. Partner with staff engineers on technical direction, code design, and systems thinking.
Set a high standard of excellence and lead by example, including in how you and your team adopt AI tools and rethink your workflows. If you're asking your engineers to embrace this shift, you'd better be living it yourself. Stay hands-on by running spikes, prototyping, and exploring ideas your team hasn't had time to chase, without taking on critical-path work.
Coach engineers to use AI as a core part of how they build: when to trust the output, when to throw it out, and how to maintain code quality when the machine is doing the typing. Teach them to fish rather than doing it for them.
Challenge your team's assumptions about how software gets made. Question old habits inherited from the era of scarce coding time (exhaustive PRDs, excessive backlog refinement, premature mockup fidelity, story-point ceremony) and encourage cheaper, faster paths to working software.
Create an environment where engineers think about the whole problem, not just the code: understanding customer needs, system dynamics, and what it takes to run software reliably in production. AI makes it dangerously easy to build the wrong thing quickly, so clear thinking about what to build matters more than ever.
What We're Looking For
An AI power user with substance and good judgment. You drive agents, have opinions about where today's models break down drawn from real experience, and you're actively rethinking what engineering management looks like when writing code is no longer the bottleneck. You help your team move fast with these tools without becoming dependent on them for the thinking. You know the difference between leveraging AI and outsourcing your brain to it.
A systems thinker. You look beyond the element at hand to the broader dynamics at play.
A strong writer and compelling storyteller. Remote work demands clear writing, clear writing is clear thinking, and clear thinking is how you get the biggest impact from AI. But clarity alone doesn't motivate people. You know how to tell the story of why the work matters, where the team is headed, and what winning looks like.
A humble, always-a-student approach to management

title: Senior Geochemist
description:
About the Company 

The mining industry has steadily become worse at finding new ore deposits, requiring >10X more capital to make discoveries compared to 30 years ago. The easy-to-find, near-surface deposits have largely been found, and the industry has chronically under-invested in new exploration technology, relying on the manual techniques of yesteryear - even as demand accelerates for copper, lithium, and other metals to build electric vehicles, renewable energy, and data centers.

KoBold builds AI models for mineral exploration and deploys those models-alongside our novel sensors-to guide decisions on KoBold-owned-and-operated exploration programs. In the eight years since founding, KoBold has become by far both the largest independent mineral exploration company and the largest exploration technology developer. Our data scientists and software engineers, who come from leading technology companies, jointly lead exploration programs with our renowned exploration geologists.

KoBold has proven its first discovery with materially less capital than the industry average and found one of the best copper deposits ever discovered: the copper is far more concentrated than the global average of copper mines, and this asset alone is expected to generate meaningful revenue for decades. KoBold has a portfolio of more than 80 other projects, each of which has the potential for another high-quality discovery.

KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

 

About the Role

KoBold explores across several continents and a widening set of commodities. This role is the geochemical capability that travels with those programs.

Reporting to the Principal Geochemist, you will work as a functioning member of exploration teams in North America, Europe, and Africa; planning and running sampling campaigns, on the ground when it matters, and turning results around quickly enough to change what the team does next.

The Principal Geochemist has responsibility for company-wide standards, independent data quality assurance, and global method and technology development. Your responsibility is in the practice, programs, field decisions, interpretation, and the day-to-day geochemical judgement that the exploration teams you work within depend on. You will work closely with data scientists and software engineers to develop new tools and drive an ever deepening analysis of results. You will work to company standards and audit against them in the field. You will be required to prioritize your time effectively across multiple projects, and multiply your reach by training field teams to sample well without you present.

 

Responsibilities

• Demonstrate in all activities a commitment to the highest standards in health and safety, environment, and community relations

• Act as the embedded geochemist for exploration programs across North America, Europe, and Africa, joining project teams for the phases where geochemical decisions are being made and providing insight to existing hypotheses and the generation of new hypotheses fast enough to influence exploration decision making

• Design geochemical sampling programs fit for the terrain, regolith, and mineral system being tested, including orientation surveys and the choice of sampling medium, horizon, size fraction, spacing, analytical suite, and digestion, across glaciated terrain, deeply weathered tropical profiles, and arid or transported cover

• Own the geochemical component of drilling programs: sampling intervals and sample support, preparation protocols, quality control insertion, and real-time review of incoming assays against the geological model

• Apply and audit KoBold's geochemical standards

title: Sr Growth Product Manager
description:
About Community Phone Company
Community Phone Company YC W19 built a simple cloud phone system for businesses that don't operate a call center.
Our solution lets a business get all modern voice features (re-route if busy, greeting menu and IVR, programmable caller ID, cloud voicemail, etc) on their existing office phone and existing employee cell phones. All employees onboard instantly, no wifi required, no app to download. Businesses should not be missing out on orders because they can only take one call at a time, and they shouldn't need an IT person in order to get a modern business phone system.
About the role
The company
Communications for the aging in America is broken. Seniors are isolated. Their families are anxious in ways that go far beyond "I hope mom's alright." James Graham started this company after seeing his own grandmother get taken advantage of by the large telecom hegemony.
They are checking her bank account daily because they cannot tell if she is being scammed. They are calling three times a day because she did not pick up and they do not know if she is okay. They are lying awake wondering if she is connected to anyone, or just sitting alone. And at the most basic level, a lot of their phone service is completely unreliable or breaks entirely for the family once she reaches a certain age.
There are 55 million Americans over 65 living at home. Most of them, and most of their families, are navigating this alone.
Community Phone is fixing that. We built a phone so simple it works out of the box, no setup required. We wrapped it with AI-powered check-in calls that surface how she is really doing. And we built a family app that replaces daily dread with genuine safety and peace of mind.
It is working. We are well into 8-figure subscription ARR, pacing to 9-figure, with 25,000+ families trusting us with something that matters deeply to them. Customers stay. They refer their friends. They tell us we took away an anxiety they had carried for years.
We are a lean, product-driven team. The people who thrive here take full ownership, are mission-driven, move quickly, and care deeply about the customer. One of our product engineers won an Oscar for best foreign film, one team member is a Thiel Fellow, one is a Harvard Philosophy PhD dropout, others are the first growth hires at now Unicorn companies, other of our product engineers are former leaders of 60+ person engineering organizations, and many are former founders.
The opportunity
We have 25,000+ families paying us every month for something they deeply value. Churn is low. NPS is high. The upsell products are built and ready.
What does not exist yet is the motion to move customers into them: the trigger identification, the experiment infrastructure, the lifecycle sequences, the in-product moments that surface the right product at the right time to a customer who already trusts us.
That is what this role builds. From scratch. Owned entirely by you. With a clear revenue target, a strong data foundation, and a direct line to product leadership and the CEO.
In year one, the PLG expansion opportunity alone is in the low millions of ARR. That is not a stretch goal requiring new customers or new channels. It is sitting in the base we already have, waiting for the right motion.
And that is just year one. The bigger picture: we are building the definitive platform for aging in place. Phone service is the wedge. Check-in calls, the family app, and products we have not built yet are the expansion. The PM who builds the upsell motion now is building the system that monetizes everything that comes after it.
What you will own

• Expansion revenue from our consumer subscriber base, measured in ARR

• The full upsell motion: trigger identification, experiment design, in-product nudges, lifecycle sequences, pricing page, and onboarding flows

• A prioritized roadmap of PLG experiments, run with shared engineering resources and a strong bias toward non-eng levers where possible

title: SAP TM S/4HANA Rollout Consultant, Netherlands
description:
SAP TM S/4HANA Rollout Consultant, Netherlands
Contract: 6 months initially, extensible. Long-term programme. Start: 1 November 2026 Location: Remote, for consultants based in the Netherlands. Day rate: EUR 400 a day. Language: English.
The programme
A global manufacturing organisation is moving its transportation processes onto SAP Transportation Management (TM) on S/4HANA. The global template is the base, and it is being rolled out to sites in waves. Each wave brings new plants, new carriers and new country requirements into the template.
You will own the TM solution for the waves you are given. You will run fit-to-standard sessions with the business, decide what the template already covers and what is a real local gap, and design the answer without breaking the global standard. You will then carry that design through build, testing, cutover and early support after go-live.
What you will work on
Fit-gap for each rollout wave. Local transport practice, carriers, legal and document needs measured against the global design. TM solution design on S/4HANA. Freight planning, carrier selection and tendering, freight order execution, charge calculation and freight settlement. Integration across the S/4HANA logistics chain. Outbound sales orders and deliveries, inbound purchasing flows, warehouse execution, and freight cost through to finance. Carrier connectivity. EDI or business network onboarding, tracking, and status messages from carriers. Functional specifications for the build team, working closely with integration, development and test leads. Test planning and defect resolution through integration and user acceptance testing. Cutover, hypercare and handover to support for each wave. Feeding what each wave teaches back into the template, so the next wave starts from a better base.
What you bring
8 or more years in SAP logistics, with SAP TM on S/4HANA as a core part of it. At least one TM rollout or global template programme for a manufacturing business, where you did the fit-gap and the solution design yourself, not only the configuration. Working knowledge of how TM connects to SD, MM, EWM and FI/CO, and where those integrations tend to break. Experience running workshops with business users and turning what they say into a design and a specification. Comfort working remotely across countries in a programme team made up of several companies.
Useful but not essential:
SAP Business Network for Logistics, or a carrier visibility platform. Both embedded and side-by-side TM deployments. Automotive, industrial or process manufacturing. Multimodal, international or dangerous goods transport. SAP TM certification.
How to respond
Apply with your CV and your available start date. With it, add three lines on your most recent TM rollout: the countries or sites in scope, whether TM was embedded or side-by-side, and what you personally designed.
About Yadimen
Yadimen Consulting Limited is an IT consulting company focused on financial services. For this programme we are putting experienced SAP TM people in front of a global manufacturing organisation.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Delivery Engineering
description:
About CircleCI Engineering
CI/CD has been solved. Now it's being reinvented. AI agents don't just run pipelines. They write code, trigger builds, interpret failures, and propose fixes. The interfaces that developers use to understand and trust that work don't exist yet. We're building them.
At CircleCI , our guiding principles aren't posters on a wall. We learn fast: we run experiments, accept failure, and scale what works. We think like the customer: every decision connects back to the developer sitting in front of a failing build at 2 am. We own the outcome: not just our slice of it, but the whole thing. If that's how you already work, you'll fit here.
About Delivery Engineering
Delivery Engineering enables CircleCI engineers to deliver quickly, confidently, and securely. We provide the tools and resources that make standard patterns and best practices simple to adopt, and we reduce toil.
Our current focus is the agentic software development lifecycle: how changes are found, planned, built, reviewed, merged, and measured as AI agents take on more of the work. We evaluate the harnesses, repository patterns, skills, and agentic tooling available, decide what our teams should standardize on, and build and support the shared tooling other teams depend on.
We're a small, very senior team, and everyone on it shapes where we go. Every improvement we make compounds across the organization.
What You'll Do

•
Build AI-natively. AI is how we work. It's not a productivity layer on top of engineering, but the default starting point for how problems get approached and solved.

•
Shape how CircleCI builds software with agents. Help define the end-to-end agentic SDLC, from identifying a change through planning, execution, pull request, merge, and measuring impact afterward. Evaluate shared tooling and patterns, and help decide what teams standardize on.

•
Start from how our teams actually work. Spend time with engineering teams to understand their workflows and where they get stuck. Use what you learn to drive decisions and direction that teams adopt because the work fits how they operate.

•
Build platforms, not one-offs. Build and support shared tooling that other teams depend on, and own its adoption as much as its delivery. A tool nobody uses isn't done.

•
Measure what matters. Instrument agent usage and outcomes so we know what improves throughput and quality and what just burns tokens. Treat cost, model choice, and reliability as design concerns.

•
Make build-vs-buy calls. Evaluate models, vendors, and open-source tools against our needs, and choose the path that gets engineers the most leverage.

•
Lead through influence. Write the design docs, lead technical discussions across teams, and mentor engineers across the org as they adopt agentic workflows.

What You'll Bring

•
Direct experience driving agentic developer experience efforts. You've driven an initiative that changed how an engineering organization builds software with AI agents. You can speak to what you built, how you measured its impact, how you drove adoption, and what didn't work.

•
Hands-on depth with agentic tooling. You work daily with coding agents, agent harnesses, MCP, and skills or prompt design. You know how to evaluate agent output and reason about model and token economics.

•
A platform mindset. You've built and supported internal platforms or developer tooling that other engineers build on and rely on, and driven their adoption.

•
Backend depth in Go. You've owned production backend services in Go, including API design, data modeling, and service integration.

•
A track record at staff scope. 8+ years of production engineering experience, including technical decisions that spanned multiple teams and accountability for whether they landed.

•
Decision-making grounded in your users. You build direction by listening first. You turn the needs of many teams into clear tradeoffs, document your reasoning, and bring people along.

title: Senior System Software Engineer - Datacenter Power Management
description:
NVIDIA is redefining accelerated computing and powering the next era of artificial intelligence. Our data-center platforms bring together GPUs, CPUs, networking, systems, and software to solve some of the world’s most exciting computing problems. We are looking for a Senior System Software Engineer to join NVIDIA ’s Datacenter Performance and Power Management Software team. You will be responsible for architecting production software for datacenter power management controllers. Your work will also cover cluster- level dynamic provisioning and power-management control system technologies for next-generation data-centers.
You will work at the intersection of hardware architecture, embedded firmware, device drivers, operating systems, and AI workloads. Your responsibilities will span the entire product lifecycle-from initial architectural design and pre-silicon validation through silicon bring-up, productization, and deployment in extensive data-center infrastructures. This is an outstanding chance to influence how next-generation NVIDIA GPUs provide top-tier performance, energy efficiency, and reliability.
What You’ll Be Doing:

• Architect, build, implement, and debug data center power and performance-management software, with particular emphasis on end-to-end power management at racks and data halls.

• Develop real-time controllers, policies, and mechanisms that dynamically optimize performance, power, thermals, and energy efficiency under demanding data-center workloads.

• Drive features across the full product lifecycle: requirements, architecture, implementation, pre-silicon validation, silicon bring-up, productization, and production support.

• Collaborate with GPU architects and hardware designers to define hardware-software interfaces and influence the power-management capabilities of next-generation processors.

• Analyze complex interactions among workloads, clocks, voltages, power limits, thermals, telemetry, and system-level policies.

• Lead the investigation and resolution of complex power, performance, stability, and reliability issues spanning firmware, drivers, hardware, and platform software.

• Develop validation strategies and automation for functional correctness, transition latency, performance-per-watt, and robustness across operating conditions.

• Build clear architecture, interface, and compose specifications for new power-management features.

• Partner with geographically distributed architecture, ASIC, firmware, driver, validation, platform, and data-center systems teams.

What We Need to See:

• BS or MS degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field-or equivalent experience.

• At least 12+ years of extensive industry experience crafting system software, embedded firmware, device drivers, or other hardware-related production software.

• Strong programming skills in C, including experience developing, debugging, and maintaining complex low-level software.

• Deep understanding of operating-system fundamentals, device-driver architecture, embedded or real-time software, concurrency, interrupt handling, and hardware programming.

• Experience interpreting hardware specifications and developing software interfaces for registers, telemetry, interrupts, and control mechanisms.

• Strong understanding of computer architecture and hardware-software interactions.

• Proven ability to independently debug complex problems across multiple software and hardware layers.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of working effectively across organizational and geographic boundaries.

Ways to Stand Out From the Crowd:

• Background with architecting, designing, or implementing datacenter provisioning, monitoring, and managing power at a CSP/NCP.

• Hands-on experience with GPU, CPU, accelerator, or SoC power and performance management.

• Background with crafting or implementing P-state selection, DVFS, clock-control, voltage-control

description:

Legal matters require specialized expertise, and each one involves its own facts, practices, parties, and institutions. title: Director of Security & Risk
description:
SentiLink https://www.sentilink.com/ helps institutions and protects customers by accurately resolving identities and flagging fraud risk. Each day, we verify more than 3 million identities, flagging 150k+ fraud attempts in the process. The problems we work on are challenging, and solving them takes deep domain expertise, rigorous analysis, and a willingness to dig into the details.

At SentiLink, you'll work alongside smart, highly collaborative colleagues who respect each other's time and judgment, take ownership, and follow through on their commitments. Together, we do truly meaningful work protecting the identities of innocent consumers and flagging the fraudsters attempting to exploit them.

We're well capitalized and growing quickly. We already serve 13 of the top 15 U.S. banks, we're expanding into new markets, and we're backed by Craft Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NYCA, and Max Levchin. We've been named to the Forbes Fintech 50 https://www.forbes.com/companies/sentilink/?list=fintech50 and as a 2026 FICO Industry Vanguard Decision Award Winner https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260330439998/en/SentiLink-Named-a-2026-FICO-Industry-Vanguard-Decision-Award-Winner-for-Leadership-in-Identity-Theft-Detection. We were also the first company to go live https://resources.sentilink.com/blog/sentilink-makes-history-as-first-ecbsv-provider with the electronic Consent Based Social Security Number Verification (eCBSV) service, and we've testified before the U.S. Congress https://resources.sentilink.com/media/dr.-david-maimons-congressional-testimony-on-emerging-fraud-threats-and-the-evolving-fraud-landscape on the future of identity.

We want SentiLink to be the best place you've ever worked. We offer generous benefits and support a range of working arrangements, from fully remote to in-office. We are a digital-first company with strong collaboration across the U.S. and India, and we meet in person regularly to build relationships. We have offices in Austin, San Francisco, New York City, Seattle (Bellevue), Los Angeles, and Chicago in the U.S., and in Gurugram (Delhi) and Bengaluru in India.

ROLE:

SentiLink's Information Security team is responsible for protecting our systems, data, and customers while enabling the business to operate securely and efficiently. We work closely with Engineering, IT, Legal, Product, and business teams to manage security risks, maintain regulatory compliance, and build effective security controls across the organization.

We're looking for a Director of Security & Risk to lead our security governance, compliance, assurance, and risk management programs. This is a leadership role with broad ownership across FedRAMP, SOC 2, PCI DSS, customer and partner security assessments, third-party risk, and security policy.

This is not a traditional GRC role. SentiLink operates a highly technical, AWS-based environment, and many of the risks and compliance requirements we manage require deep technical understanding. We're looking for someone who can independently evaluate technical risks, understand security architecture and proposed remediations, and work effectively with engineers, auditors, regulators, and business stakeholders.

You will lead and develop a team of security and compliance professionals, establish priorities, identify gaps in our existing programs, and develop a roadmap for improving our security posture. We expect you to bring the experience and judgment to identify problems and opportunities independently, rather than simply execute an existing plan.

You will report to SentiLink's security leader and work closely with Security Engineering, which remains a separate function responsible for technical security architecture and implementation.

Success in this role means building a proactive, effective, and scalable security program that goes beyond passing audits to meaningfully reducing organizational risk.

This is a remote, US-based position.
